data.summary: With parallel=fixed and max_parallel_tasks=20 (local layer), ddflow status prints 'parallel: 9 (fixed: ceiling 20; limited by demand (8 in flight))' next to '582 more are ready but held by the parallelism cap'. The config doc says fixed is a ceiling lowered only under load and restored; why_not_higher in core/flowcontrol.py reports demand whenever in-flight is under the limit, so the line names no reason for 9 instead of 20, and next offered only 2 items although the operator raised the limit to 20 (D-swarm-push-2026-11-05).
data.title: Fixed-mode parallel limit sits below its ceiling and blames demand while hundreds of ready items are held

data.body:
Fixes bug B69323fd23e: With parallel=fixed and max_parallel_tasks=20 (local layer), ddflow status prints 'parallel: 9 (fixed: ceiling 20; limited by demand (8 in flight))' next to '582 more are ready but held by the parallelism cap'. The config doc says fixed is a ceiling lowered only under load and restored; why_not_higher in core/flowcontrol.py reports demand whenever in-flight is under the limit, so the line names no reason for 9 instead of 20, and next offered only 2 items although the operator raised the limit to 20 (D-swarm-push-2026-11-05).

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B69323fd23e --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B69323fd23e --regression-test <test>` first).

data.body:
Single writer per item; no private queues. Research docs/ddflow/research/swarm-orchestration.md; proposal docs/ddflow/decisions/swarm-orchestration.md. Start only after SW-decide has recorded the D-SW-* answers (SW-decide is not in needs on purpose, L-needs-on-decide-tasks).

AMENDED by D-swarm-answers (SW-Q2, operator 2026-10-24): the scheduler MAY also LAUNCH lanes itself from operator-approved templates, not only answer pulls; launching stays bound by D-agent-parity consent and the approved-template registry, with an audit event per launch. SW-decide recorded the answers.

RELATED 2026-11-01: OPT-swarm-unify moves score.py behind OptimizerPort after this lands; no edge in front of this task. Keep choose/pull pure so the move is a registration.

AMENDED 2026-11-05 (D-swarm-pilot-2026-11-05): DX-fleet-registry edge cut, fleet.py has no family, trust or price. Globs widened: next is declared in surfaces/declared/lifecycle/navigate.py. SW-pull is the pure choice; DX-dispatch-plan calls it later.

COORDINATOR CALLS 2026-11-05 (coordinator, not operator decisions): (1) Dispatch note: `next --lane` returns the note text and stays read-only (r-read-verbs-read-only); `claim` records it. (2) Globs: add ddflow/api/__init__.py, the ddflow/api/lifecycle/ files actually touched, and goldens, as literal files, not directories. (3) Lane data: family and trust come from the lane's template and the model catalog (DRV-model-catalog); no template or an unknown value returns unavailable and offers nothing, never a default; no dependency on DX-fleet-registry. Unblocking: globs set to dispatch.py and its test so the pure part proceeds while sw-stopproto holds lifecycle/; surface files are added with `update --add-globs` once free, and a refusal there is a wait, not repeated. This is a coordinator exception to the lane brief's 'do not work around a conflict': the pure code does not touch the leased files.
